title: US arrests: the machine peaked in 1997
unit: Estimated arrests per year, millions (FBI; excludes traffic)
note: US arrests peaked in 1997 at 15.28 million — a fact most readers do not know — and 2024 is 51% below that. Drug arrests peaked separately in 2006 (1.89M) and remain the largest single category. Constant across the whole era: 82–84% of all arrests are for lesser, non-index offences. Sparse points are drawn as points, not smoothed into a line the data cannot support; dotted stretches are years that are not Tier A. The sweeping operations in the register above — the World Cup's 905 arrests against HSI's 2,545 for all of FY2024 — sit inside these annual millions, which is the scale a headline arrest number should be read against.
publisher: FBI CIUS/CDE; Council on Criminal Justice corroborating

series.name: All arrests
series.basis_short: FBI estimated arrests, all offences, excluding traffic
caveats: Selected years, not a continuous annual series — the FBI's own estimates for the years shown, one consistent series (never mixed with the BJS 1980-2009 series, which uses different weights and yields ~11.6M for 1997).
2016 and 2021 are known national data gaps and are not shown.
An arrest is an enforcement action, not a conviction; 82-84% of arrests across this whole period are for lesser (Part II) offences.

series.name: Drug arrests
caveats: Peaked in 2006 at 1,889,810; 2024 (822,488) is still the largest single arrest category.
1980 and 2006-2008 values corroborated via compilations of FBI Table 29 (Tier B where marked).

themes.statement: Criminal arrests peaked in 1997 at 15.3 million; 2024, at 7.5 million, is 51% below that.

This chart counts CRIMINAL arrests reported by police agencies. The sweeping arrests in DHS announcements are mostly civil 'administrative arrests' under immigration law — a separate counting system that never enters these figures. Both are true at once: criminal arrests falling while administrative immigration arrests surge (95,629 by ICE ERO in under five months of 2025 alone).
The series ends at 2024 — before the 2025–26 enforcement surge. A national 2025 criminal-arrest figure does not exist yet.

Where sweep cases meet courts: of 33 known federal defendants charged with non-immigration crimes in Chicago's Operation Midway Blitz, 25 were cleared — dismissals, grand juries refusing to indict, one acquittal — against 2 guilty pleas (tracker as of Aug 2026).

accuracy_note: About the accuracy of these figures: arrest totals are estimates assembled from agency reports, and two official federal series disagree with each other (see the data-quality register). 2016 and 2021 are national data gaps. Civil immigration arrests are counted separately by DHS and never appear in this chart. Every figure is as published by its source on the access date recorded in the source register.
